sections.h2: Which Moore County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
One department covers every step in Moore County, from listing and appraisal through billing and collection. Visit the Historic Courthouse at 1 Courthouse Square, Carthage, NC 28327, any weekday between 8 am and 5 pm, or call 910-947-2255. Post Office Box 457 in Carthage takes mail.

The county's Tax page splits the work into divisions that follow the state statutes. Listing keeps ownership records and personal property accounts, and Appraising values land and buildings. Collecting has a current section for bills in their normal window and a delinquent section for past-due accounts.

  • Send the coupon from your bill by post, pay at the counter, or pay on the county's online page.
  • Phone 1-855-451-2620 with your bill numbers in hand.
  • Walk-in payers may use cash, checks or bank cards.
  • Credit cards and electronic checks run through InvoiceCloud, which adds a convenience fee for the cardholder.

Ask the Tax Department whether any town or district bill applies to your address in addition to the county bill.

sections.h2: How valuable are homes in Moore County?
sections.html:
The county's population reached an estimated 110,619 by mid-2025, a 10.9% rise from the 2020 base, over a land area of 697.68 square miles.

The 2020-2024 housing numbers show why assessment values matter to owners here.

  • Half of owner-occupied homes are valued above $351,400.
  • Households that own where they live: 76.4%.
  • Total housing units by mid-2025: 52,979.
  • Typical household income: $86,080.
  • Average trip to work: 26.6 minutes.

With a typical home valued in six figures, even a small percentage error in the tax value repeats every year. Read your property record card against the house as you know it.

sections.h2: When does a Moore County tax bill turn late?
sections.html:
Bills fall due each September 1. State law sets the grace period in G.S. 105-360: a payment made before January 6 owes no interest, and a later one adds 2% through the end of January, then 0.75% a month.

January is also the listing season for personal property. Personal property, including business equipment, is listed each year, and real estate is listed permanently once it is on the books (G.S. 105-307). Statewide, owners list in January, with the window closing on the 31st unless an extension applies.

A fall sale does not cancel that year's bill. Ask the closing attorney whether the tax will be prorated or paid in full out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: How often is Moore County revalued?
sections.html:
Moore County revalues every four years. Its latest revaluation became effective January 1, 2023, and its FAQ schedules the next for 2027, then every fourth year, unless the market or state law calls for another timetable.

That beats the state floor of one reappraisal every eight years, and counties may shorten the cycle by resolution (G.S. 105-286).

Values come from mass appraisal using the cost, market and income approaches, fixed to January 1 of the revaluation year. They do not follow the market between revaluations. An appraiser may still visit after a building permit, a parcel map change, or a recorded sale priced well away from the assessment. Permit data flows in from the county plus Aberdeen, Pinebluff, Pinehurst and Southern Pines.

Added heated floor area is an improvement, as are decks, porches, patios, storage buildings, pools and barns, and the owner is expected to report them.

sections.h2: How does a Moore County value challenge work?
sections.html:
Send the Tax Department a signed written request or the county appeal form. For real estate the window opens each January 1 and shuts when the county's review board adjourns, a date the county advertises in the local newspaper.

Moore County appeal paths by property type
Property typeWhen to appealHow
Real propertyOpens January 1, ends at board adjournmentSigned request or appeal form, informal review first, then the board
Personal property, business or notThirty days counted from the bill dateSigned written request or personal property form
Registered motor vehicleThirty days counted from the bill dateSigned written request; pay the bill on time regardless

You must show that the value is higher than surrounding properties justify, or higher than fair market value, using cost, sales or income evidence from the run-up to the revaluation date.

If the board rules against you, the next stop is the state-level Property Tax Commission, which needs written notice filed within thirty days after the decision is mailed (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What tax relief can Moore County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
Three state programs can reduce the bill on a permanent residence, and an owner can draw on only one. Moore County owners apply through the county tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled homestead exclusion: whichever is bigger, a flat $25,000 or one half of appraised value, comes off the taxable amount for an owner who has reached age 65, or who is totally and permanently disabled, within the income limit (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran homestead exclusion: $45,000 of value is excluded, with nothing asked about age or income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is capped at 4% of income for owners at or under the limit, or 5% for incomes up to 150% of it, and the excess is deferred as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

The state revenue department lists, for 2026, $38,800 as the income limit and $58,200 as the 150% mark. Form AV-9 goes to the county, ideally during listing, and the county must accept it up to June 1 before that tax year starts.

A sale or move triggers repayment of the circuit breaker deferral for the prior three fiscal years, so include it in the closing payoff.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Moore County house that still has tax due?
sections.html:
Yes, but the tax follows the parcel, so it is settled at closing. A lien for real property tax attaches on the listing date (G.S. 105-355), and the county can enforce it by foreclosure, which is described in G.S. 105-374.

A tax foreclosure runs like a mortgage foreclosure action in the county court. The house is sold at auction on the courthouse steps, and an owner may still redeem ahead of confirmation by paying the tax with its penalties and costs.

Selling before that point usually costs less. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff, look for any open town bill, and hand the figure to the closing attorney.

sections.h2: How does Moore County set the value of a particular house?
sections.html:
Every parcel is valued under the 2023 Schedule of Values adopted by the Board of Commissioners, using the features the house had on January 1 of the year in question. The appraiser records those features on a Field Review Document, and owners can pull that document or a shorter property record card from the county GIS site or from the Tax Department.

The land records team builds the ownership side from the paperwork that reaches the recorder's counter or the Clerk of Court, and it also keeps the parcel data that the GIS maps display. Mass appraisal means one set of standard methods is applied to a whole group of properties, then tested statistically. No single appraiser sets a price house by house.

  • Check the square footage, bedroom and bath counts and outbuildings on your card.
  • Look at what similar houses on your street are valued at.
  • Bring sales, cost or income evidence if you disagree, since the proof rests on you.
  • Remember that a recorded sale far from the assessment can trigger a visit.

For a seller, a clean card means fewer surprises when a buyer's agent compares your tax value to the contract price.

faqs.a: You can pay at the Carthage courthouse counter, through the mail, on the county website, or over the phone at 1-855-451-2620. The counter takes cash, checks and plastic, and card payments add a convenience fee.

faqs.q: What year did the last Moore County revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2023. The county has the next one scheduled for 2027, with four-year rounds after that.

faqs.q: How long can I contest a vehicle or personal property value?
faqs.a: The window is thirty days from the bill's date. Send a signed written request to the Tax Department, and pay a vehicle bill on time anyway so no late penalty builds.

faqs.q: Do Moore County values rise and fall with the market each year?
faqs.a: No. The county fixes value on the revaluation year's January 1 date and leaves it alone in between. New improvements can still draw an appraiser and change the figure.

faqs.q: Who accepts the elderly or disabled exclusion application?
faqs.a: With the county tax office, on Form AV-9. The state prefers it during January listing but takes it up to June 1 before the new tax year starts, and a household can use just one of the three programs.
